items.title: Google Cloud Warns Three AMD Turin CPU Flaws Could Leak Data Across Processes in VMs
items.description: Google Cloud VMs on AMD Turin chips need a guest OS patch and a stop-and-start to protect against three CPU side-channel flaws, Google said this week. The company has already applied mitigations against attacks between VMs, and between VMs and the host. items.title: Calendar Invites and Live Proxies: Inside a Google Session Hijacking Campaign
items.description: Since mid-August 2026, a phishing operation has been stealing live Google sessions from corporate users. Every check defenders normally lean on to judge a link came back clean, and the operator designed it that way on purpose. The Threat Research team at Material Security spotted the campaign and has since taken down hundreds of attacker domains in an effort the team calls Operation CloudFire.

items.title: Notion Customer Data Compromised in Fireworks AI Hack
items.description: The attackers accessed chat transcripts for fewer than 1% of Notion workspaces. Most transcripts were unattributable. The post Notion Customer Data Compromised in Fireworks AI Hack appeared first on SecurityWeek.

items.title: Inside an AI Attack Against a US Retailer
items.description: When hand-typed commands failed to breach a US retailer, the attacker turned to AI-generated scripts, achieving lateral movement in minutes.

items.title: Hackers plant GSocket on Linux servers for persistent access
items.description: Multiple threat actors are abusing GSocket, a legitimate open-source remote access tool, to maintain access to Linux servers even after patching the vulnerabilities exploited to gain initial access. [...]

items.title: Critical Red Hat Quay Vulnerability Could Expose Private Container Images
items.description: Attackers could exploit a critical Red Hat Quay flaw to steal private container images, overwrite repositories and maintain persistent access. The post Critical Red Hat Quay Vulnerability Could Expose Private Container Images appeared first on SecurityWeek.

items.title: Chinese AI Project Scouts Spies in Taiwan Chip Industry
items.description: The CCP built a Big Data system to scrape reams of information and learn about individuals abroad, to potentially target and exploit them. Think Alice Huang Lite.

items.title: Japan Pushes Emergency Funding for Cybersecurity as AI-Assisted Breaches Rise
items.description: The package adds public-private cyber responders, an AI-focused team run by the economic ministry, and more leeway to use the government's new active cyber-defense powers.
